note: Phylogenomic matrices of sampled gastropods reject Orthogastropoda; remaining deep nodes depend on matrices and models.
authorsVerbatim: Zapata, F.; Wilson, N.G.; Howison, M.; et al.

title: A multi-gene phylogeny of Cephalopoda supports convergent morphological evolution in association with multiple habitat shifts in the marine environment
note: Multigene topology and mapped habitats for sampled living cephalopods; fossil lineages and ancestral ecology remain outside direct sampling.
authorsVerbatim: Lindgren, A.R.; Pankey, M.S.; Hochberg, F.G.; Oakley, T.H.

title: Allonautilus: a new genus of living nautiloid cephalopod and its bearing on phylogeny of the Nautilida
note: Living Allonautilus anatomy compared with Nautilus and selected fossils; Nautilida evidence cannot bound the broader historical Nautiloidea route.
authorsVerbatim: Ward, P.D.; Saunders, W.B.

title: Ammonoids across the Permian/Triassic boundary: a cladistic perspective
note: Cladistic analysis of sampled boundary-crossing ammonoids; it addresses survival and turnover near one interval, not the full Ammonoidea range.
authorsVerbatim: McGowan, A.J.; Smith, A.B.

title: The Lazarus ammonoid family Goniatitidae, the tetrangularly coiled Entogonitidae, and Mississippian biogeography
note: Family-level early Late Viséan material and biogeographic synthesis within Goniatitida; it supports that regional study window but cannot define the whole order’s endpoints.
authorsVerbatim: Korn, D.; Klug, C.; Mapes, R.H.

title: Origin of the Ceratitida (Ammonoidea) inferred from the early internal shell features
note: Comparative internal-shell analysis infers ceratitid relationships and explicitly states an Early Permian–end-Triassic order range; inferred ancestry and continuous occupancy remain unclaimed.
authorsVerbatim: Shigeta, Y.; Zakharov, Y.D.; Mapes, R.H.

title: The phylogeny of Hildoceratidae (Cephalopoda, Ammonitida) resolved by an integrated coding scheme of the conch
note: Integrated conch-character matrix for 105 Early Jurassic Hildoceratidae taxa; it supports that family study window rather than the order’s complete history.
authorsVerbatim: Bardin, J.; Rouget, I.; Cecca, F.

title: Molecular clocks indicate turnover and diversification of modern coleoid cephalopods during the Mesozoic Marine Revolution
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Fossil-calibrated molecular clocks for sampled modern coleoids; posterior ages are model estimates, not fossil first appearances.
authorsVerbatim: Tanner, A.R.; Fuchs, D.; Winkelmann, I.E.; et al.

title: Bayesian inference reveals a complex evolutionary history of belemnites
note: Tip-dated morphological analysis of 24 sampled belemnites with published first/last occurrence inputs and a 253.1 Ma origin offset; topology and node ages remain model- and calibration-dependent.
authorsVerbatim: Stevens, K.; Pohle, A.; Hoffmann, R.; Immenhauser, A.

title: A mitogenomic phylogeny of chitons (Mollusca: Polyplacophora)
note: Mitogenomic topology from newly sequenced and public chitons; mitochondrial sampling and fossil-calibration ambiguity bound deep inference.
authorsVerbatim: Irisarri, I.; Uribe, J.E.; Eernisse, D.J.; Zardoya, R.

title: Phylogenomics of Aplacophora (Mollusca, Aculifera) and a solenogaster without a foot
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Phylogenomic analysis of sampled solenogasters and caudofoveates; the legacy Aplacophora label is retained as a historical navigation grade, not assumed to be an exact natural group.
authorsVerbatim: Kocot, K.M.; Todt, C.; Mikkelsen, N.T.; Halanych, K.M.

title: Early jawless vertebrates and cyclostome origins
note: Review distinguishes the 358 Ma undoubted lamprey record, probable Late Carboniferous hagfish record and older molecular divergence; it does not identify a direct cyclostome ancestor or exact crown origin.
authorsVerbatim: Janvier, P.

title: Molecular Dating of the Teleost Whole Genome Duplication (3R) Is Compatible With the Expectations of Delayed Rediploidization
note: Concatenated ohnologue clocks estimate intervals for crown Actinopterygii, Neopterygii, Holostei, Teleostei and major teleost lineages; every interval is model- and calibration-dependent, not a fossil FAD.
authorsVerbatim: Qi, M.; Clark, J.; Moody, E.R.R.; Pisani, D.; Donoghue, P.C.J.

title: Multi-locus phylogenetic analysis reveals the pattern and tempo of bony fish evolution
note: A 21-locus, 24-calibration relaxed-clock study estimates a 409 Ma mean split between living coelacanth and lungfish-plus-tetrapod lineages; the estimate is not a fossil first appearance.
authorsVerbatim: Broughton, R.E.; Betancur-R, R.; Li, C.; Arratia, G.; Ortí, G.

title: Conodonts: Past, present, future
note: Systematic review identifies the upper Cambrian through Triassic biostratigraphic record while warning that element-based taxonomy and incomplete multielement reconstruction complicate one stable biological range.
authorsVerbatim: Sweet, W.C.; Donoghue, P.C.J.

title: Origins and relationships of Paleozoic coral groups and the origin of the Scleractinia
note: Systematic review whose abstract explicitly separates the Early Ordovician–end-Permian Tabulata, Middle Ordovician–end-Permian Rugosa and Middle Triassic–Holocene Scleractinia records.
authorsVerbatim: Oliver, W.A., Jr.

title: Stromatoporoids and extinctions: A review
note: Review distinguishes two major stromatoporoid-grade episodes and warns against treating the intervening gap as one continuous clade range.
authorsVerbatim: Kershaw, S.; Jeon, J.

title: Diversification of early ferns
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, Section B: Biological Sciences
note: Review questions attribution of Devonian taxa to ferns while treating Lower Carboniferous filicalean evidence as substantially firmer.
authorsVerbatim: Galtier, J.; Scott, A.C.

title: An araucarian conifer bract-scale complex from the Lower Jurassic of Massachusetts: implications for estimating phylogenetic/stratigraphic congruence in the Araucariaceae
note: Open article describing specimen J 1430 from the Hettangian South Hadley Falls Member and identifying it as a bona fide Araucariaceae megafossil.
authorsVerbatim: Axsmith, B.J.; Escapa, I.H.; Huber, P.

title: Dinosaur coprolites and the early evolution of grasses and grazers
note: Reports diagnostic grass phytolith morphotypes from latest-Cretaceous Lameta Formation dinosaur coprolites; affinity and depositional age remain the limiting evidence.
authorsVerbatim: Prasad, V.; Strömberg, C.A.E.; Alimohammadian, H.; Sahni, A.

title: Exceptional continental record of biotic recovery after the Cretaceous–Paleogene mass extinction
note: Corral Bluffs stratigraphic synthesis includes a 65.35 Ma fossil fruit and leaflets assigned to Leguminosae in Figure 3J–K.
authorsVerbatim: Lyson, T.R.; Miller, I.M.; Bercovici, A.D.; Weissenburger, K.; Fuentes, A.J.; Clyde, W.C.; Hagadorn, J.W.; Butrim, M.J.; Johnson, K.R.; Fleming, R.F.; et al.

title: The origin of the legumes is a complex paleopolyploid phylogenomic tangle closely associated with the Cretaceous–Paleogene (K–Pg) mass extinction event
note: Phylogenomic analysis explicitly identifies the 65.35 Ma Corral Bluffs material as the oldest unequivocal legume fossil while keeping divergence estimates model-dependent.
authorsVerbatim: Koenen, E.J.M.; Ojeda, D.I.; Bakker, F.T.; Wieringa, J.J.; Kidner, C.; Hardy, O.J.; Pennington, R.T.; Herendeen, P.S.; Bruneau, A.; Hughes, C.E.

title: Early Ordovician sea scorpions from Morocco suggest Cambrian origins and main diversification of Eurypterida
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Primary description of unequivocal upper Tremadocian Fezouata eurypterids; the approximately 479 Ma occurrence is a fossil-record bound, not a lineage origin date.
authorsVerbatim: Van Roy, P.; Richards, M.A.; Ortega-Hernández, J.

title: Distribution and dispersal history of Eurypterida (Chelicerata)
note: Systematic distribution review records a Late Permian Russian occurrence at approximately 250 Ma while noting incomplete taxonomy and sampling.
authorsVerbatim: Tetlie, O.E.

title: Zygoptera systematics: past, present, and future
note: Systematic review distinguishes the oldest Serpukhovian Odonatoptera record from the later appearance of modern Odonata.
authorsVerbatim: Sutherland, K.K.; Carter, B.E.; Abbott, J.C.; et al.

title: Odonata (dragonflies and damselflies) as a bridge between ecology and evolutionary genomics
note: Review identifies Saxonagrion minutus at approximately 268 Ma as the earliest modern odonate; this is a fossil minimum rather than an origin estimate.
authorsVerbatim: Bybee, S.; Córdoba-Aguilar, A.; Duryea, M.C.; et al.

title: Induced Power Scaling Alone Cannot Explain Griffenfly Gigantism
note: Functional study summarizes the reviewed first Namurian B record and persistence through at least the end of the Middle Permian; it does not supply an exact extinction date.
authorsVerbatim: Ellers, O.; Gordon, B.; Hukill, A.; et al.

title: Revision of Permo-Carboniferous griffenflies based upon new species and redescription of selected poorly known taxa from Eurasia
note: Systematic redescription of selected griffenfly material; it does not establish exact genus-wide temporal endpoints for Meganeura.
authorsVerbatim: Nel, A.; Fleck, G.; Garrouste, R.; et al.

title: Early evolution of beetles regulated by the end-Permian deforestation
note: Integrated fossil dataset identifies Early Permian Tshekardocoleidae as the earliest definite beetles and uses a standardized Asselian bin beginning at 298 Ma.
authorsVerbatim: Zhao, X.; Yu, Y.; Clapham, M.E.; et al.

title: Evolving perspectives in Hymenoptera systematics: Bridging fossils and genomes across time
note: Systematic review treats the approximately 242–237 Ma xyelid record as the oldest undisputed hymenopteran fossil minimum, not an order-origin date.
authorsVerbatim: Zhang, Y.M.; Bossert, S.; Spasojevic, T.

title: Exceptionally Preserved 450-Million-Year-Old Ordovician Ostracods with Brood Care
note: Primary description identifies Luprisca as the first unequivocal pre-Silurian ostracod record and cautions against older shell-only assignments.
authorsVerbatim: Siveter, D.J.; Tanaka, G.; Farrell, Ú.C.; et al.

title: Early Evolution of Phyllocarid Arthropods: Phylogeny and Systematics of Cambrian-Devonian Archaeostracans
note: Phylogenetic and systematic treatment supporting a middle–late Cambrian phyllocarid record.
authorsVerbatim: Collette, J.H.; Hagadorn, J.W.

title: The evolutionary history of Stomatopoda inferred from molecular data
note: Fossil-calibration table treats phyllocarids as the oldest malacostracan record at at least 500 Ma; the value is not a crown-divergence date.
authorsVerbatim: Van Der Wal, C.; Ahyong, S.T.; Ho, S.Y.W.; Lo, N.

title: The Global Fossil Record of Chilopoda
note: Global catalog identifies Upper Silurian Crussolum from Ludford Lane at approximately 418 Ma as the oldest chilopod record.
authorsVerbatim: Cadenas-Amaya, O.; Riquelme, F.; Hernández-Patricio, M.; Cupul-Magaña, F.G.

title: Reconciling Divergent Ages for the Oldest Recorded Air-Breathing Land Animal
note: Geological age review dates Kampecaris obanensis to 425.5 ± 4.5 Ma; uncertainty remains separate from the display edge.
authorsVerbatim: Brookfield, M.E.; Catlos, E.J.; Garza, H.

title: The Silurian-Devonian fossil record of the Myriapoda
publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
note: Review regards pre-Pridoli records as questionable and recognizes reliable Diplopoda in the latest Silurian to Lower Devonian.
authorsVerbatim: Almond, J.E.; Lawson, J.D.

title: A Larval Sea Spider from the Upper Cambrian Orsten of Sweden, and the Phylogenetic Position of Pycnogonids
note: Primary study proposes Cambropycnogon as the oldest pycnogonid/chelicerate record; subsequent review leaves its assignment uncertain.
authorsVerbatim: Waloszek, D.; Dunlop, J.A.

title: New insights into the Devonian sea spiders of the Hunsrück Slate
note: Table 1 classifies Cambropycnogon only as possibly Pycnogonida, requiring a contested total-group interpretation.
authorsVerbatim: Sabroux, R.; Garwood, R.J.; Pisani, D.; Donoghue, P.C.J.; Edgecombe, G.D.

title: Fossil spiders
note: Systematic fossil-record review supports the Carboniferous spider record while retaining taxonomic and sampling limits.
authorsVerbatim: Selden, P.A.; Penney, D.

title: Almost a spider: a 305-million-year-old fossil arachnid and spider origins
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Study distinguishes the 305 Ma stem-like Idmonarachne from true spiders and traces Araneae to approximately 315 Ma.
authorsVerbatim: Garwood, R.J.; Dunlop, J.A.; Selden, P.A.; et al.

title: Evolutionary trends in Triceratops from the Hell Creek Formation, Montana
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
note: A stratigraphically controlled Hell Creek skull sample documents cranial character variation; proposed evolutionary mode remains sensitive to taxon and character treatment.
authorsVerbatim: Scannella, J.B.; Fowler, D.W.; Goodwin, M.B.; Horner, J.R.

title: Mites as fossils: forever small?
note: Review catalogs more than 260 mite fossils from approximately 410 Ma onward and rejects unsupported Ordovician and Permian assignments.
authorsVerbatim: Sidorchuk, E.A.

title: Aglaophyton major, a non-vascular land-plant from the Devonian Rhynie Chert
publisher: Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society
note: Primary re-examination of new and historical material that established Aglaophyton for the former Rhynia major and revised its reconstruction and conducting-strand interpretation.
authorsVerbatim: Edwards, D.S.

title: Transfer cells in Horneophyton lignieri illuminate the origin of vascular tissues in land plants
note: Open-access primary study of 24 Horneophyton-bearing sections; three NHMUK slides were selected for white-light and confocal imaging plus three-dimensional modelling.
authorsVerbatim: Kenrick, P.; Long, E.J.

title: A high-precision U–Pb age constraint on the Rhynie Chert Konservat-Lagerstätte: time scale and other implications
note: Open repository version records an ID-TIMS U–Pb zircon age of 411.5 ± 1.3 Ma from andesite in the Rhynie Outlier; the atlas uses the uncertainty interval only as a locality-age bound.
authorsVerbatim: Parry, S.F.; Noble, S.R.; Crowley, Q.G.; Wellman, C.H.

title: Galeaspid anatomy and the origin of vertebrate paired appendages
note: Primary description of articulated Tujiaaspis material from the Huixingshao Formation; CFD lift results are model outputs and do not measure whole-animal swimming performance.
authorsVerbatim: Gai, Z.; Li, Q.; Ferrón, H.G.; Keating, J.N.; Wang, J.; Donoghue, P.C.J.; Zhu, M.

title: Broad snouted cladoselachian with sensory specialization at the base of modern chondrichthyans
note: Open-access primary description of Maghriboselache mohamezanei from several Moroccan Famennian specimens, including CT-preserved neurocrania and a time-calibrated phylogenetic analysis; a 2024 correction is noted by the publisher.
authorsVerbatim: Klug, C.; Coates, M.I.; Frey, L.; Greif, M.; Jobbins, M.; Pohle, A.; Lagnaoui, A.; Haouz, W.B.; Ginter, M.

title: A new operculate symmoriiform chondrichthyan from the Late Mississippian Fayetteville Shale (Arkansas, United States)
note: Primary description and CT-based phylogenetic study of the partial holotype AMNH FF 20509; the specimen supplies direct evidence for an endoskeletal operculum but not a complete body or clade-wide range.
authorsVerbatim: Bronson, A.W.; Pradel, A.; Denton, J.S.S.; Maisey, J.G.

title: A complete insect from the Late Devonian period
note: Primary description of the nearly complete Strudiella devonica specimen from Upper Devonian freshwater sediments at Strud, Belgium; the original study interpreted it as an insect.
authorsVerbatim: Garrouste, R.; Clément, G.; Nel, P.; Engel, M.S.; Grandcolas, P.; D'Haese, C.; Lagebro, L.; Denayer, J.; Gueriau, P.; Lafaite, P.; Olive, S.; Prestianni, C.; Nel, A.

title: Is Strudiella a Devonian insect?
note: Primary re-investigation of Strudiella that rejects the original insect identification and cautions against interpreting poorly preserved Devonian arthropods as insects.
authorsVerbatim: Hörnschemeyer, T.; Haug, J.T.; Béthoux, O.; Beutel, R.G.; Charbonnier, S.; Hegna, T.A.; Koch, M.; Rust, J.; Wedmann, S.; Bradler, S.; Willmann, R.

title: Under cover at pre-angiosperm times: A cloaked phasmatodean insect from the Early Cretaceous Jehol biota
note: Primary description of one female and two male Cretophasmomima melanogramma specimens from the Yixian Formation, dated to approximately 126 ± 4 Ma, including the stem-Phasmatodea diagnosis and proposed leaf mimicry.
authorsVerbatim: Wang, M.; Béthoux, O.; Bradler, S.; Jacques, F.M.B.; Cui, Y.; Ren, D.

title: Saxonagrion minutus nov. gen. et sp., the oldest damselfly from the Upper Permian of France (Odonatoptera, Panodonata, Saxonagrionidae nov. fam.)
note: Primary description of Saxonagrion minutus from the Upper Permian Salagou Formation in the Lodève Basin, France; it attributes the fossil to Panodonata from preserved wing venation.
authorsVerbatim: Nel, A.; Fleck, G.; Béthoux, O.; Gand, G.; Lapeyrie, J.; Garric, J.

title: Catalogue of Life 2026-08-20 (COL26.8), ChecklistBank dataset 316115
version: COL26.8 released 2026-08-20; ChecklistBank dataset 316115
note: Pinned checklist source for accepted usage identity and parent classification; it is not a fossil-range, wild-distribution or biological-trait source.
authorsVerbatim: Catalogue of Life

title: Fathering style influences health outcome in common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus) offspring
note: Primary study of offspring survival and growth among common marmosets housed at the Wisconsin National Primate Research Center. Only the captive-colony comparison is summarized; it does not estimate wild behavior or distribution.
authorsVerbatim: Ziegler, T.E.; Sosa, M.E.; Colman, R.J.

title.en: Ziegler, Sosa & Colman (2017). Fathering style influences health outcome in common marmoset offspring.
title.zh: Ziegler、Sosa 与 Colman（2017）：父亲照料方式与普通狨幼体健康结果。

title: Losing its ground: A case study of fast declining populations of a ‘least-concern’ species, the bonnet macaque (Macaca radiata)
note: Primary study supporting bounded forest occupancy, temple/tourist-site history, Mysore roadside counts and a local conservation recommendation. Each finding retains its place, time and sample limits; none is a current range-wide assessment. Article states CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Erinjery, J.J.; Kumar, S.; Kumara, H.N.; Mohan, K.; Dhananjaya, T.; Sundararaj, P.; Kent, R.; Singh, M.

title.en: Erinjery et al. (2017), roadside, forest and human-use sites in southern India
title.zh: Erinjery 等（2017）：印度南部道路、森林与人类活动地点

title: Activity and Habitat Use of Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes verus) in the Anthropogenic Landscape of Bossou, Guinea, West Africa
version: Published 2017-01-30; volume 38, pages 282–302
note: One-year field study of the wild Pan troglodytes verus community at Bossou, Guinea. Study claims are bounded to the sampled site and focal individuals. Article license and attribution were checked from the University of Kent repository record; the dossier paraphrases findings and reproduces no figures or tables. CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Bryson-Morrison, N.; Tzanopoulos, J.; Matsuzawa, T.; Humle, T.

title: Primates, Provisioning and Plants: Impacts of Human Cultural Behaviours on Primate Ecological Functions
version: Published 2015-11-04
note: Primary study of one 64-individual rhesus macaque troop at Buxa Tiger Reserve, India, from October 2013 to September 2014. Ecological comparisons are limited to that troop and study-defined seasonal provisioning periods; the article states CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Sengupta, A.; McConkey, K.R.; Radhakrishna, S.

title: Male morphological traits are heritable but do not predict reproductive success in a sexually-dimorphic primate
version: Published 2019-12-24
note: Primary study measuring a selected Cayo Santiago free-ranging cohort in 2015. Heritability conclusions are bounded to the sampled pedigree, measured traits and models; the article states CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Kimock, C.M.; Dubuc, C.; Brent, L.J.N.; Higham, J.P.

title: Road-based line distance surveys overestimate densities of olive baboons
version: Published 2022-02-02
note: Primary study of road-transect surveys and sleeping-site comparison for wild olive baboons at Lake Manyara National Park, Tanzania, from 2011 to 2019. The authors report poor fit for detection models and caution that road use may bias density estimates. The article states CC BY 4.0; the summary is paraphrased.
authorsVerbatim: Kiffner, C.; Paciência, F.M.D.; Henrich, G.; Kaitila, R.; Chuma, I.S.; Mbaryo, P.; Knauf, S.; Kioko, J.; Zinner, D.

title: Segmental morphometrics of the olive baboon (Papio anubis): a longitudinal study from birth to adulthood
version: First published 2017-03-14
note: Longitudinal body-morphometry study of 14 female and 16 male captive olive baboons at the CNRS Primatology Station in Rousset-sur-Arc, France. The source record identifies CC BY 4.0; the summary is paraphrased and does not reproduce figures or tables.
authorsVerbatim: Druelle, F.; Aerts, P.; D’Août, K.; Moulin, V.; Berillon, G.

title: Contrasting effects of male immigration and rainfall on rank-related patterns of miscarriage in female olive baboons
version: Published 2021-02-17
note: Primary observational study of wild olive baboons in Gombe National Park, Tanzania, using reproductive and miscarriage records from 1972 to 2002. The article states CC BY 4.0; its conditional associations are not evidence of a species-wide rate or deliberate causation.
authorsVerbatim: Bailey, A.; Eberly, L.E.; Packer, C.

title: Pre-Historic and Recent Vicariance Events Shape Genetic Structure and Diversity in Endangered Lion-Tailed Macaque in the Western Ghats: Implications for Conservation
version: Published 2015-11-11
note: Primary mitochondrial-DNA study using wild Western Ghats samples, with separately identified captive samples in some analyses. Claims are bounded to sampled sites and markers; the article states CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Ram, M.S.; Marne, M.; Gaur, A.; Kumara, H.N.; Singh, M.; Kumar, A.; Umapathy, G.; et al.

title: Changing ecologies, shifting behaviours: Behavioural responses of a rainforest primate, the lion-tailed macaque Macaca silenus, to a matrix of anthropogenic habitats in southern India
version: Published 2020-09-23
note: Primary field study of one habituated, free-ranging troop in Puthuthottam, Valparai plateau, Tamil Nadu, during February–May 2016. Findings are bounded to one troop, one forest fragment and the dry season; the article states CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Dhawale, A.K.; Kumar, M.A.; Sinha, A.

title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of rabies and habitat suitability of the common marmoset Callithrix jacchus in Brazil
version: Published 2022-03-31
note: Primary analysis of Brazilian Ministry of Health passive surveillance from 2008 to 2020 and a presence-based habitat-suitability model. Reported cases, observed localities and modeled suitability are distinct evidence; none is a species-wide census or complete range inventory. Article text is item-level verified CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Benavides, J.A.; Raghavan, R.K.; Boere, V.; et al.

title: Mitogenomic phylogeny of Callithrix with special focus on human transferred taxa
version: Published 2021-04-06
note: Primary Callithrix mitogenomic study combining 49 newly sequenced mitogenomes with published sequences. The approximately 0.51 Ma estimate concerns sampled mitochondrial lineages under the study model, not a nuclear-genome species tree or definitive species-origin date. Article text is item-level verified CC BY 4.0.
authorsVerbatim: Malukiewicz, J.; Cartwright, R.A.; Curi, N.H.A.; et al.

title: Homo sapiens-specific evolution unveiled by ancient southern African genomes
version: Published online 2025-12-03; issue date 2026
note: Primary whole-genome study of 28 ancient southern African individuals dated 10,200–150 calibrated years before present. Genetic comparisons are bounded to the study samples and comparison panel, not a species-wide survey. Article text is item-level verified CC BY 4.0; summaries are paraphrased and figures, third-party content and data files are not reused.
authorsVerbatim: Jakobsson, M.; Bernhardsson, C.; McKenna, J.; et al.

title: The ecology, subsistence and diet of ~45,000-year-old Homo sapiens at Ilsenhöhle in Ranis, Germany
version: Nature Ecology & Evolution 8(3):564–577; version of record published 2024-01-31
note: The article-level CC BY 4.0 study uses stable isotopes from 10 human and 52 animal remains at one cave; its diet inference is not a species-wide Homo sapiens profile. No article expression, figures, third-party content or data files are reproduced.
authorsVerbatim: Smith, G.M.; Ruebens, K.; Zavala, E.I.; et al.

title: Effect of human feeding on the road mortality of Rhesus Macaques on National Highway-7 routed along Pench Tiger Reserve, Madhya Pradesh, India
version: Journal of Threatened Taxa 3(4):1656–1662; published 2011-04-26
note: One-year monitoring of one 11-km NH-7 segment in Madhya Pradesh. The paper front page identifies CC BY 3.0 Unported and separately states non-profit reuse with attribution; the dossier paraphrases facts and reuses no article expression or figures.
authorsVerbatim: Pragatheesh, A.
